title: COVID-19 ARTIC v3 Illumina Library Construction and Sequencing Protocol
author: DNA Pipelines R&D
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bibtkann
materials: Primer pool sequences (v3) can be found here: https://github.com/joshquick/artic-ncov2019/blob/master/primer_schemes/nCoV-2019/V3/nCoV-2019.tsv Where an alt primer is available, the non alt version is omitted. Achieving more even genome coverage A hypothetical 'ideal' multiplex primer pool would generate the same number of reads from each amplicon, so the fraction of reads due to each amplicon would be 1/n, where n is the number of primer pairs in the multiplex pool. In reality this is not achievable, and the fraction of reads observed for each amplicon varies widely. The ratio [actual observed read fraction/‘ideal’ read fraction] can be calculated for each individual amplicon, as indicated by the differently-coloured dots on the box-and-whisker plots below. This tells us whether a particular amplicon is under-represented (ratio <1x) or over-represented (>1x). By changing the weights of each primer pair within the primer pool (' rebalancing ') the number of reads obtained for each amplicon can be modified, and the effect of the process is illustrated below. The plots show the distribution per amplicon prior to rebalancing primer pair concentrations (above) and after (below). More amplicons cluster around 1x after rebalancing and the distance between the maximum and minimum ratios is also markedly reduced. Weight to apply per primer pair A more detailed description of the process is provided in this document: Improving the evenness of SARS-CoV-2 genome coverage by titration of primer concentration (final).pdf NEB Q5® Hot Start High-Fidelity 2X Master Mix New England Biolabs Catalog #M0494L Prepare the following mastermixes: PCR Primer Pool 1 Master Mix Vol/PCR RXN (µl) Vol/96 plate (µl) inc. excess Q5 Hotstart 2X Master Mix 12.5 1440 Primer Pool 1 (11µM total) 3.6 415 Nuclease-free water 6.9 795 Total 23 2650 PCR Primer Pool 2 Master Mix Vol/PCR RXN (µl) Vol/96 plate (µl) inc. excess Q5 Hotstart 2X Master Mix 12.5 1440 Primer Pool 2 (10.8µM total) 3.6 415 Nuclease-free water 6.9 795 Total 23 2650 The equivolume primer pools used in the standard protocol are of 10 micromolar (µM) cumulative concentration, therefore each of the 98 primers in each pool is at 102 nanomolar (nM) in the pool and at 15 nanomolar (nM) in the final reaction. With the rebalanced primer pools, for equivalency we dilute them such that the average primer concentration is 102 nanomolar (nM) , and therefore the average concentration of each primer in the final reaction is also 15 nanomolar (nM) . Mix thoroughly by vortexing.

We use the NEB NEBNext® Ultra™ II DNA Library Prep Kit for Illumina, which we have automated on the Agilent Bravo platform with some modifications. 200ng is our standard input for library preparation, an acceptable range is 50ng – 1ug per sample. We use a custom adapter set, however any TruSeq adapters are suitable. NEBNext Ultra II DNA Library Prep Kit for Illumina - 96 rxns New England Biolabs Catalog #E7645L
The plate is incubated on deck at 20 °C for 00:15:00 , however this step may also be performed on a thermocycler.

We use KAPA HiFi HotStart ReadyMix and unique dual indexed (UDI) tag plates for library PCR. Note: this deviates from the standard NEB protocol which uses NEBNext Ultra II Q5 Master Mix and different cycling conditions. 2x Kapa HiFi Hotstart Readymix Kapa Biosystems Catalog #KK2602 Prepare PCR mastermix On ice : KAPA PCR Mastermix Vol/PCR RXN (µl) Vol/96 plate (µl) inc. excess KAPA HiFi HotStart ReadyMix 25 3000 Water 12.5 1500 Total 37.5 4500 Mix well by pipetting.

Equivolume pools may be quantified either by qPCR or on an Agilent Bioanalyzer. Pools are then diluted to 1nM for sequencing. qPCR Quantify samples in triplicate using the KAPA Complete kit (Universal) for Illumina (KK4824) plus the KAPA Library Quantification Dilution Control (KK4906). We use the SPT Labtech Mosquito LV to stamp library pools in triplicate into a 384 assay plate, and the Agilent Bravo to setup the qPCR reactions (1:1600 dilution). qPCR is performed on the Roche LightCycler 480. Agilent Bioanalyzer Prepare 3 dilutions of the equivolume pool (1:10, 1:100, 1:1000). Run 1µl of each dilution in triplicate using the High Sensitivity DNA assay kit. Confirm size distribution is as expected, check there is no primer-dimer or adapter-dimer present.

steps.title: Decontaminate workspace and keep cold
steps.instruction: Decontaminate bench surfaces, pipettes and gloves with RNase ZAP in an RNase‑free pre‑PCR environment; keep all reagents and samples chilled (on ice) throughout the procedure.

steps.title: Thaw RNA plate
steps.instruction: Place the 96‑well PCR plate containing 10 µL extracted RNA on ice to thaw.

steps.title: Prepare LunaScript RT master mix
steps.instruction: In a UV‑treated pre‑PCR area, prepare RT master mix per reaction: 4 µL LunaScript SuperMix, 6 µL nuclease‑free water (total 10 µL per reaction, 1152 µL for 96 reactions); vortex thoroughly to mix.

steps.title: Dispense RT master mix
steps.instruction: Using the SPT Labtech Dragonfly Discovery, dispense 10 µL RT master mix into each well of the RNA plate (which already contains 10 µL RNA).

steps.title: Seal, centrifuge and run RT program
steps.instruction: Seal the plate, briefly centrifuge, then run the thermocycler program: 25 °C 10 min, 55 °C 20 min, 95 °C 1 min, hold at 4 °C indefinitely; lid temperature tracking enabled.

steps.title: Store cDNA (pause point)
steps.instruction: Store the resulting cDNA at 4 °C the same day or at –20 °C for up to one week.

steps.title: Dispense primer‑pool master mix
steps.instruction: Use the Dragonfly Discovery to add 19 µL primer‑pool master mix to each well of two 96‑well plates.

steps.title: Add cDNA to primer pools
steps.instruction: Using the Agilent Bravo, add 6 µL cDNA template to each primer‑pool reaction and mix (use filtered tips to reduce aerosol contamination).

steps.title: Heat‑seal and run multiplex PCR
steps.instruction: Heat‑seal the plates, place on a thermocycler and run: 98 °C 30 s, 95 °C 15 s, 65 °C 5 min; repeat steps 2‑3 for a total of 35 cycles; hold at 4 °C indefinitely. Gradient PCR is recommended; annealing may be optimized to 63 °C.

steps.title: Store amplified cDNA (pause point)
steps.instruction: Store amplified cDNA at 4 °C overnight or at –20 °C for up to one week.

steps.title: AMPure XP bead cleanup of amplified cDNA
steps.instruction: Allow AMPure XP beads to equilibrate to room temperature (~30 min) and ensure the suspension is homogeneous. Centrifuge amplified cDNA plates at 1000 × g, RT, 1 min. Combine primer 1 and primer 2 reactions per sample into one plate. Add 0.8× volume SPRI beads (40 µL beads to 50 µL cDNA), mix and incubate 5 min at RT. Place on magnet for 2 min, discard supernatant, wash beads twice with 180 µL 75 % ethanol (30 s each), remove ethanol. Resuspend beads in 20 µL nuclease‑free water, incubate 3 min RT, magnet 5 min, transfer supernatant (purified cDNA) to a new plate. Store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Quantify purified cDNA with AccuClear
steps.instruction: Prepare standards: pipette 20 µL each DNA standard into wells A1‑G1 of a PCR plate, add nuclease‑free water to H1. Dilute AccuClear dye 100× to working concentration by mixing 300 µL dye with 30 mL buffer, vortex, load into a 384‑well reservoir. Using the Mosquito LV, stamp 200 nL amplified cDNA and 1 µL of each standard (triplicate) into a 384‑well assay plate. Using the Bravo 384ST, add 50 µL 1× AccuClear dye to each well and mix. Measure fluorescence on a BMG FLUOstar Omega plate reader. If any sample >125 ng/µL, dilute with nuclease‑free water to 10‑125 ng/µL and repeat assay. Ensure each 20 µL sample contains 2.5‑50 ng/µL before library preparation.

steps.title: End‑prep reaction
steps.instruction: On ice, prepare end‑prep master mix per 96‑well plate: 1.2 µL Ultra II End Prep Enzyme Mix, 2.8 µL Ultra II End Prep Reaction Buffer (total 4 µL per reaction, 480 µL for 96). Mix well. Using the Bravo, add 4 µL master mix to each well containing 20 µL purified cDNA, mix. Seal and thermocycle: 20 °C 30 min, 65 °C 30 min, hold at 4 °C.

steps.title: Adapter ligation reaction
steps.instruction: On ice, prepare ligation master mix per 96‑well plate: 12 µL Ultra II Ligation Master Mix, 0.4 µL Ligation Enhancer, 1 µL 10 µM TruSeq adapter (total 13.4 µL per reaction, 1608 µL for 96). Mix well. Bravo adds 13.4 µL to each end‑prep reaction and mixes. (If using NEB adapters, follow NEB protocol to add USER enzyme.) Perform a 0.8× SPRI bead cleanup: add 0.8× beads, incubate 5 min RT, magnet 2 min, discard supernatant, wash twice with 180 µL 75 % ethanol (30 s each), elute in 25 µL nuclease‑free water, incubate 3 min RT, magnet 5 min, transfer 25 µL eluate to a new plate; use 12.5 µL of this eluate for library PCR.

steps.title: Library PCR amplification
steps.instruction: Add 37.5 µL PCR master mix and 12.5 µL sample (from the ligation eluate) into each well of a lyophilised UDI plate, mix thoroughly. Seal and thermocycle: 95 °C 5 min; then 4 cycles of 98 °C 30 s, 65 °C 30 s, 72 °C 2 min; then 72 °C 5 min; hold at 4 °C.

steps.title: Pool libraries
steps.instruction: In a post‑PCR lab, combine 5 µL of each of the 96 library PCR products into a low‑volume reservoir using a multichannel pipette, mix, and transfer the pooled volume to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Bead cleanup of pooled library
steps.instruction: Equilibrate AMPure XP beads ~30 min at RT; add 0.8× beads to the pooled library, mix and incubate 5 min RT. Place tube on magnet for 5 min, discard supernatant. Wash beads twice with 1 mL 75 % ethanol (30 s each) and remove ethanol. Resuspend beads in 1 mL elution buffer, mix, incubate 3 min RT. Magnet 5 min, transfer supernatant (final library) to a new tube.

steps.title: Prepare NovaSeq sequencing reagents
steps.instruction: Defrost Illumina NovaSeq SP SBS and cluster reagent cartridges for 2‑4 h in a room‑temperature water bath; blot excess water with a lint‑free tissue, invert gently 10×, and tap the bottom to release bubbles. Defrost DPX1, DPX2 and DPX3 components from a NovaSeq XP‑2 lane kit, keep on ice. Bring the flow cell to room temperature (~10 min) before use.

steps.title: Denature and neutralize pooled library
steps.instruction: For each SP lane, take 18 µL of 1 nM pooled library, add 4 µL 0.2 N NaOH, vortex briefly, and incubate at room temperature for 8 min. Add 5 µL 400 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0 to neutralize, vortex briefly, and keep on ice.

steps.title: Prepare ExAmp master mix
steps.instruction: On ice, combine per SP flow cell: 126 µL DPX1, 18 µL DPX2, 66 µL DPX3 (total 210 µL). Vortex 30 s, briefly centrifuge (≤280 × g, RT). Use the mixture within 1 hour of preparation.

steps.title: Combine ExAmp mix with library
steps.instruction: Add 63 µL ExAmp master mix to each denatured library tube and mix well.

steps.title: Prepare instrument for loading
steps.instruction: Ensure the NovaSeq instrument is washed, waste containers are emptied, and the system is ready for use before loading libraries.

steps.title: Load flow cell and start run
steps.instruction: Place the flow cell into the dock with the 2‑lane manifold clamped. Pipette 80 µL of the library + ExAmp mix into each manifold well, wait ~2 min for the solution to fill the lane. Start the sequencing run within 30 min of loading. Unclamp the manifold and discard it, load the flow cell onto the NovaSeq stage, and load the SBS and cluster reagent cartridges.
